name.en: Japanese Envoy Ship to Tang China

type: ocean-going sailing ship (RECONSTRUCTION; no wreck or drawing survives)
schema_notes: level_m = deck height above the waterline. Every layout element is a RECONSTRUCTION based on the 2010 Heijo Palace replica.

basis.fact: Full-scale replica displayed at Heijo Palace Site for the 2010 1300th anniversary; now at 朱雀門ひろば, free to board
Replica: length 30 m, beam 9.6 m, displacement 300 t, cargo 150 t
Replica built by Okamura shipyard, Matsuzaki (Izu)
From the 8th mission (717), 4 ships became the norm: ambassador on ship 1, vice-ambassador on ship 2, judges and recorders on ships 3 and 4; only once did all 4 return
Crew organisation: sailing crew (captain, navigator, sailors, soldiers) vs passengers (envoys, students, monks)
Nara Prefecture document on the replica

rooms.name: Masts and mat sails
rooms.purpose: 2 masts with bamboo mat sails (網代帆)

flooding.watertight_subdivision: Unknown. If Chinese-built style is assumed, transverse bulkheads (reconstruction).

sequence: Wrecked in headwinds after landing south of Baekje; drifted to a southern island

game_sinking_hooks: Storm: waves flood the deck; shipwrecks were common

uncertain: Everything is reconstruction; the replica's design basis is not documented in the sources reached (picture scrolls such as 吉備大臣入唐絵巻 and 鑑真和上東征絵伝 are commonly cited but unverified)
